title: no-test-regression rubric incorrectly fails spec-required test edits and legitimate count-assertion updates
description: The no-test-regression rubric fires as a failure on test file changes that are legitimately required, producing false QA gate failures across multiple runs. Three distinct cases observed: (1) A new additive test added to patch_file_tests.rs as mandated by the spec was flagged as a regression. (2) Count assertions (e.g. standard_registry_has_expected_tool_count) that must increment when a new tool is registered fail the rubric even though the change is correct. (3) Tests modified to match new spec-mandated behaviour (not to silence failures) are rejected. The rubric cannot distinguish spec-required changes from bad-faith test silencing. This signal consolidates 3e5f9c2a, c6e8a0b2, and f5d8a3b2.
proposed_resolution: Amend the no-test-regression rubric criterion to include a safe-harbour clause: test file changes are permitted when (a) the spec explicitly requires the test change, OR (b) the change is a count/registry assertion updating a hardcoded value that tracks a resource added by the spec, OR (c) the change adds a new test (additive only, no deletions or modifications to existing assertions). Bad-faith silencing: modifications to existing assertions that weaken them without a corresponding spec requirement remain prohibited. The rubric should require the agent to cite the relevant spec requirement when invoking the safe-harbour.
